query: uh mobile phone battery swollen in one week shopkeeper shouting at me not replacing uh 12000 rupees gone

model_output.summary: You bought a mobile phone for Rs. 12,000 and its battery swelled up within one week. The shopkeeper is refusing to replace it and shouting at you. Because your dispute amount is Rs. 12,000 (which is under 50 Lakhs), you can file a complaint at the District Consumer Commission under the Consumer Protection Act.
facts_extracted: Mobile phone battery swelled within one week of purchase
Cost of the phone is Rs. 12,000
Shopkeeper refused replacement and shouted at the buyer

options.title: File Consumer Complaint
options.description: File a formal complaint at the District Consumer Commission since the value of the goods is Rs. 12,000, which is well below the Rs. 50 Lakhs limit.
pros: Can seek replacement or refund for defective goods
cons: Takes time and requires proper documentation like purchase bills

options.title: Approach District Legal Services Authority
options.description: Seek help from the District Legal Services Authority to resolve the pre-litigation dispute or refer it to a Lok Adalat.
pros: Helps reach a quick compromise or settlement
cons: Depends on the willingness of the shopkeeper to settle
options.forum: District Legal Services Authority / Lok Adalat

citations.relevance: Grants jurisdiction to the District Consumer Commission for complaints where the value of goods does not exceed Rs. 50 Lakhs, fitting your Rs. 12,000 phone purchase.
Provides for organizing Lok Adalats to help settle pre-litigation disputes amicably.

missing_info: Do you have the original purchase bill or invoice for the phone?
Did you contact the authorized service center of the mobile brand?
